messages.author: 706a0969d0cf5307
messages.subject: Add thinning interval to monitor()?
parts:
Could you add thinning interval as an argument to rstan's monitor() function? 

I think this will affect the effective sample size estimate and Rhat.

Context:

I have multiple MCMC chains. Some were obtained with STAN. Some were obtained with other software.

I want to calculate effective sample size and Rhat in the same way for all the chains. I decided to use the rstan way (instead of the coda way) of calculating effective sample size and Rhat.

Tangent: coda's gelman.diag() function gives an Rhat that differs from rstan's summary() and monitor() functions for some reason. coda's summary() function also gives a Monte Carlo SE that differ's from se_mean from rstan's summary() function. 

The non-STAN code outputted thinned samples. To use monitor() on those samples to get MC SE and Rhat, I want to be able to tell monitor() the thinning interval.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Add thinning interval to monitor()?
parts:
On Saturday, December 31, 2016 at 3:33:58 PM UTC-5, Qian Zhang wrote:

Could you add thinning interval as an argument to rstan's monitor() function?
Easily, but we don't think it is a good idea. Thinning the draws to be analyzed just reduces the effective sample size and increases the uncertainty in the inferences.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Add thinning interval to monitor()?
parts:
On Saturday, December 31, 2016 at 5:42:48 PM UTC-5, Qian Zhang wrote:
Thanks.

I realize that thinning reduces the effective sample size, but I have to cope with someone else's software, which thins by default. Also thinning could be necessary if you don't have space to store all samples.

If storeage is a problem, you can thin the chains by specifying the thin argument to sample() or stan(). But thinning after you have already stored them is just sacrificing information for no gain.

The fact that other software thins by default and Stan doesn't already tells you a lot about the respective dependence among adjacent draws. If NUTS is going well and you were to thin to every fifth draw, the retained draws will be indistinguishable from independent. But your effective sample size would be about half as much as it would be if you didn't thin.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Add thinning interval to monitor()?
parts:
Also, what exactly do you expect a thinning argument to the Rhat and 
ESS calculations would do?  As you lose all of the information you thinned
there is no correction for that loss — the best you can do is compute Rhat
and ESS using all of the samples that you kept.

Note also that Stan uses a more robust calculation for Rhat and ESS that
splits each chain, so even without thinning the results from Stan and coda
will not in general be the same.  Empirically the coda results tend to miss
many of the pathologies that the Stan results catch.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Add thinning interval to monitor()?
parts:
I assume a package would just literally thin then calculate
everything based on the thinned sample.

If you need to save space, thin before you save the draws (as
an argument to the Stan call in whatever interface you're using).
Otherwise, the space all gets allocated anyway, and thinning
afterward just loses information as Ben and Michael were saying.

CmdStan's a bit different --- it streams the draws out to a file.
But again, you can thin before you stream to save space.

- Bob
